title: Fresh Mint and Dark Chocolate Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Fresh mint steeped in the dairy instead of vanilla; cocoa and melted dark chocolate make a chocolate base; chocolate pieces folded in.
summary: A deep chocolate custard ice cream made the classic French way, but with fresh mint steeped into the dairy and chopped dark chocolate folded through at the end. Cool, herbal and properly chocolatey.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa), chopped into small pieces

steps.title: Steep the mint
steps.text: Bring the cream and milk just to steaming, stir in the mint leaves, cover and leave for 30 min. Sieve, pressing hard on the leaves, and pour the minty dairy back into the pan; fresh leaves give a softer, greener flavour than extract.

steps.title: Make a cocoa paste
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, sugar and cocoa in the heatproof bowl until there are no dry specks. Mixing cocoa with the yolks first stops it clumping in the hot liquid.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Rewarm the mint dairy until steaming, whisk a ladle into the cocoa paste, then a second, and tip everything back into the pan. The gradual heat keeps the yolks from setting into lumps.

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Stir over low heat for 5-8 min, scraping the corners, until it coats the spatula and reads 77-80 °C. Never let it bubble, or it will turn grainy.

steps.title: Melt in chocolate
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and add the 100 g finely chopped chocolate with the salt. Leave for a minute so the residual heat softens it, then stir until glossy.

steps.title: Cool the base
steps.text: Strain into a bowl sitting in the iced water and stir until cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 h. Chocolate bases thicken as they chill, which helps a smooth churn.

steps.title: Churn with pieces
steps.text: Churn until thick, then add the chocolate pieces for the final minute. Cold custard sets the chocolate instantly, so it stays in crisp little shards.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container, press baking paper onto the surface and freeze for at least 4 h before serving.

tips: Use only leaves, not stalks, which can taste bitter and grassy.
A common mistake is steeping the mint too long or boiling it; keep it covered off the heat for 30 min for a clean flavour.
Chop the folding chocolate small; large chunks freeze rock hard.
Spearmint gives a gentle, sweet flavour; peppermint is sharper and cooler.
storage: Keep frozen in the covered container for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 5-10 min at room temperature before scooping.
